titulo: Indirect object pronouns: Direct or indirect? Verbs and false friends

aula.objetivo: Use indirect object pronouns (me, te, le, nos, os, les) with verbs like dar, decir, escribir, regalar, prestar, and preguntar, distinguish the direct object from the indirect object, and avoid false friends like «apellido», «pegar», «prestar», and «regalar».

sessao.titulo: Direct or indirect? Verbs and false friends

blocos.titulo: Direct or indirect, and false friends
blocos.explicacao: STEP 1: to decide between the two pronouns, ask the verb. "What? Whom?" points to the direct object («lo, la»). "To whom? For whom?" points to the indirect object («le, les»). «Escribí una carta» answers what was written; «Le escribí una carta» also answers to whom. STEP 2: verbs that almost always take an indirect object: dar, decir, escribir, contar, preguntar, responder, pedir, prestar, enseñar, ofrecer, regalar, explicar, mostrar, mandar, enviar, and also «gustar, interesar, encantar, doler, parecer». «Me duele la cabeza» (my head hurts — literally, the head hurts to me). STEP 3: verbs that take a direct object when it's a person: llamar, ayudar, esperar, visitar, invitar, escuchar, ver, conocer. «La llamo», «Lo ayudo». STEP 4: «preguntar» and «responder» take the indirect object, unlike how English sometimes treats them: «Le pregunté su nombre» and «Le respondí ayer» — English "I asked her" and "I answered him" look like direct objects, but Spanish treats the person as indirect here. STEP 5: «pedir» also takes the indirect object for the person being asked: «Le pedí un café al camarero». «Pedir prestado» means to borrow; «prestar» means to lend, not to render a service: «Le pedí prestado el coche» and «Le presté el coche». STEP 6: false friends: «apellido» is last name/surname, not nickname, which is «apodo» or «mote»: «Mi apellido es Rosa; mi apodo es Rosi». «Regalar» means to give as a gift, and «un regalo» is a gift — not a perk or a pleasure. «Pegar» means to hit or to glue, not to catch: «Le pegó a su hermano» means "he hit his brother". «Enseñar» means to teach and also to show: «Me enseñó su casa» means "he showed me his house". STEP 7: in Latin America, word order and the pronouns stay the same; what changes is «os», which doesn't exist there. Instead of «os escribo», you say «les escribo».
blocos.comparacao: English also keeps direct and indirect objects distinct in form sometimes («I saw her» versus «I gave her the book»), but everyday speech blurs the line by letting a single pronoun like "her" do double duty in both roles. Spanish keeps the split sharp no matter the context: «la vi» (direct) and «le di» (indirect) never swap. The false friends in this part can trip up an English speaker in a very specific way: «apellido» isn't close to a nickname, «prestar» has nothing to do with being "prestigious", and «pegar» has nothing to do with "pegging" something — it means to hit or stick.

tabela.exemplo: [misto] Mi apellido es Rosa, mi apodo es Rosi.

erros.motivo: «Preguntar» takes the indirect object for the person.

erros.errado: [misto] Mi apellido es Pepe. (meaning to say: nickname)
erros.motivo: «Apellido» means last name; the nickname is «apodo».

erros.errado: [misto] Pegué el coche a mi hermano. (meaning to say: I lent)
erros.certo: [misto] Le presté el coche a mi hermano.
erros.motivo: «Pegar» means to hit or to glue; to lend is «prestar».
The pronoun comes before the verb.

blocos.enunciado: Write out, and say out loud, at least eight sentences about what you asked to borrow, lent, and asked friends or colleagues this week. Use «pedí prestado», «presté», «pregunté», «dije», and «escribí», always with «le» or «les».
Mentally conjugate «yo, tú, él, nosotros, vosotros, ellos» with the indirect object pronouns: «me, te, le, nos, os, les». Say a sentence with each one.
